speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly how many days old your baby is and when the bilious vomiting first started? Also, has your baby passed any stool or gas since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the infant have any visible skin abnormalities like a sac-like protrusion on the lower back, and was there any swelling noted in the perianal area at birth? Additionally, have you noticed any signs of respiratory distress or difficulty feeding beyond the vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray. I need to check for dilated bowel loops and the "double bubble" sign to differentiate between potential causes like duodenal atresia.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_X-ray Findings: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction. Rectal_Biopsy Histopathology: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease. Vital Signs: Temperature 37.5°C (99.5°F), Heart Rate 145 bpm, Respiratory Rate 40 breaths/min. Abdominal Examination: Noticeable distension, decreased bowel sounds, tympanic sound indicating gas, firm and distended abdomen with palpable bowel loops and signs of discomfort.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing an absence of ganglion cells confirm the diagnosis of Hirschsprung's disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease.
